name: Textarea
summary: Lets people enter or edit several lines of text.
description: A textarea collects free text that may run over several lines: a message, a description, a comment, an address. It shows a chosen number of lines, scrolls beyond them and can be resized. It has a visible label above, an optional description and, when its value fails validation, a message under it. One line of text is a Text field.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
The editable box: the native multi-line text control, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the value, shows the placeholder while empty and as many lines as the rows property.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.
Text saying what the severity means (what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, what was confirmed), associated with the control as a description. Shown only with a severity.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, value text and inline padding take the height, the text size and the inline padding of the Button of the same size; the label takes the text size of the value; the description and the message take the helper sizes.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (28 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (44 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty, in a lighter color. It disappears when people type: never the label, never an instruction people must remember.

properties.name: Rows
properties.description: Number of text lines visible before the control scrolls; people can resize it vertically.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What the severity means: what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, or what was confirmed. Shown with a severity, in the color of that severity, and replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Read-only
properties.description: The value can be read, focused and copied but not edited (a generated identifier). Say so in the label or the description.

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. Replaces the invalid boolean: error, warning and success are the three severities of a form control (decision forms-severity); information that holds before any check is the description's job.

options.description: No severity: nothing was checked, or there is nothing to say (default).
The value is not accepted: the border takes the error color, the message says what is wrong and how to fix it, and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).
The value is accepted but deserves attention: the border takes the warning color and the message says what to check. No web state: said in the message text.
The value was checked and confirmed: the border takes the success color and the message says what was confirmed. No web state: said in the message text.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.

Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the focus color as a 2.4 px outline drawn flush over its border however it was focused; the border and the text do not move.

Severity error: the box is filled with the subtle error background, on hover too, an outline in the error color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the error color.

Severity warning: an outline in the warning color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the warning color. No web state beyond the data attribute.

Severity success: an outline in the success color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the success color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Not editable: the box takes the level 1 surface; the value stays focusable and selectable.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.

Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius (2 px at small, 4 px at medium and large, as the Button's) comes from it too; the border width does not change.
The block padding sets the inset of the first and last lines; the control grows with the rows property and can be resized vertically.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name. The placeholder is exposed as a placeholder and used as a name only when nothing else names the control, which never happens here.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.

guidelines.text: Expose the textbox role, the name, the value and the required, read-only, disabled and error states through the platform's native multi-line text control, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.
Use the native textarea element: it exposes the textbox role as multi-line, with its value and states, without ARIA.
Every field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically; help text that people need to fill the field (format, example) is visible too, as the description.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id; reference the description and the message with aria-describedby, so they are read after the name.
The placeholder is a short hint, never the label and never an instruction: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
Show a hint in a text field to help communicate its purpose; because placeholder text disappears when people start typing, include a separate label describing the field.
Apple's recommended minimum text size is 11 pt on iOS and iPadOS; the 12 pt text of the description and the message is above it.

Say the severity in text next to the field, whatever it is: the message names what is wrong and how to fix it for an error, what to check for a warning and what was confirmed for a success, and is associated with the control. Color is never the only sign of a severity.

Say that the value is in error with aria-invalid="true" on the control, for the error severity only, and that a field is required with the required attribute, which the browser exposes as required. The web has no state for a warning or a success: the message says them, and aria-invalid is never set for them.
Mark required fields in the label or the description, never by the error color alone.

Label, value, description and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1, message text in its severity color: error 6.12:1 and 7.06:1, warning 13.01:1 and 11.17:1, success 7.87:1 and 7.89:1 (on every surface level the lowest are error 5.79:1 in light mode and 5.30:1 in dark mode, warning 12.30:1 and 8.38:1, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1). On the error fill (global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default, at rest and on hover), the value is 16.91:1 and 11.67:1 and the placeholder 5.42:1 and 6.62:1. Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 3.30:1 (light) and 6.40:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest (3.12:1 and 4.80:1 at the lowest, on the surface levels 1 and 3 in light mode and level 3 in dark), 3.12:1 and 5.86:1 against the hover fill on the default surface; the severity borders and outlines (the accent functional border): error 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, warning 3.27:1 and 8.09:1, success 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 on the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 (error), 3.09:1 and 6.07:1 (warning), 7.44:1 and 4.57:1 (success) on every surface level; the focus outline 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. The outlines are drawn over the border, on the surface around the field, so they are checked against it. Against the error fill, the other color next to it, the error border is 5.45:1 (light) and 5.14:1 (dark). Disabled is exempt. A warning border on the subtle warning fill, which a field may take as its fill in step 6, is 2.95:1 in light mode: a known shortfall (issue #119).

A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus: a 2.4 px outline in the focus color drawn flush over the border, at every size, so focus is visible by pointer and keyboard alike (WCAG 2.4.7). WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) is not met at 1x and 2x, because the part of the outline over the border changes contrast only 2.21:1 in light and 1.13:1 in dark, and the fields do not claim it.

The focus outline is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard. It is a CSS outline, never a box-shadow, so forced colors mode repaints it in a system color.

The severity outline (1.2 px) and the focus outline (2.4 px) differ by width, so a field with a severity is not mistaken for a focused one, in forced colors too, where both take the same system color. At 1x the severity outline is as wide as the 1 px border at rest: the severity's color and the message say what the severity is, never the color alone.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 28, 36 and 44 pixels.

The label, description and message are set from 12 to 16 px, under the large text size of the contrast criterion (18 pt, about 24 px), so their colors keep 4.5:1. WCAG sets no minimum text size: it asks that text resize up to 200 % without loss of content or functionality, which the box allows because its height is a minimum that grows with larger text.

Fields that collect information about the person (name, email, phone, address) carry the matching autocomplete token, so browsers and assistive technology can identify their purpose. The template passes it through its extra attributes.
A read-only field keeps its value focusable and selectable and is exposed as read-only; a disabled field leaves the focus order. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

A read-only field looks almost the same as an editable one (its fill is 1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill): say that it is read-only in the label or the description, not by the fill alone.

Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the small and medium sizes (28 and 36 pt) fall under it on iOS today and the large size (44 pt) reaches it: the Figma library has no platform heights.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; all three sizes (28, 36 and 44 dp) fall under it on Android today. Expose an error with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label is a noun phrase naming the information asked for: Message, Description, Delivery notes. Sentence case, no colon, no trailing punctuation.
The description says what to include, or a length limit, when it helps: Up to 500 characters.
The placeholder, when any, is a short example, never an instruction and never the label.
The message of an error says what is wrong and how to fix it: Enter a message of at least 20 characters.

props.label: Notes

decisions.text: The box of a field in error is filled with global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default (textarea.control.background.error): #FEECEA in light mode, #2B0B08 in dark mode, at rest and on hover alike, under the error border and outline. Read-only and disabled keep their own fills. The value, the placeholder, the label, the description and the message keep their colors. It follows the Text field (decision same-box-as-text-field).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 (#103 step 12, point 1, also the reference rendering of the Forms foundation step 6) between two options, measured on every size, at rest, on hover and with focus, light and dark, surface levels 0 to 3: A, global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default at rest and its hover step global.bg.subtle.functional.error.hover on hover; B, the subtle error fill at rest and on hover alike (chosen). In light mode A's hover fill (#FCCDC6) brings the placeholder to 4.33:1, under the 4.5:1 of WCAG 1.4.3; with B every pair passes: placeholder 5.42:1 (light) and 6.62:1 (dark), value 16.91:1 and 11.67:1, the error border and outline against the fill 5.45:1 and 5.14:1, against the surface levels 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 at the lowest. The fill is solid, as the team validated in the Forms foundation step 5; the hover tint it gives up was 1.05:1 from rest, and the Figma prototype, whose error fill is the same #FEECEA, has no hover in error. The value and the placeholder keep their roles (global.text.on-base.neutral.primary and .tertiary): the on-subtle neutral role has a single step, which cannot tell the placeholder from the value.

decisions.text: The Textarea follows the Text field's decision variants-modeled-differently, which holds the departures from the Figma prototype, the measurements and the options: the `value` property instead of the `filled` state, the platform's caret, `severity` with `message`, the `description`, an always visible label, and read-only kept. It adds the same guideline: a read-only field looks almost the same as an editable one (1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill), so say that it is read-only in the label or the description, not by the fill alone. The read-only example and the readonly property say so. No token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the model and record; B, A plus the read-only guideline (chosen); C, read-only styled as rest, rejected because it would remove the only visual cue and is a breaking change. See the Text field's decision for the reasoning.

decisions.text: The placeholder of the Textarea is global.text.on-base.neutral.tertiary in every enabled state (textarea.control.placeholder-color.default) and global.text.state.disabled.default when disabled, as the Text field's (decision placeholder-tertiary of the Text field, which holds the rule, the options and the measurements). The decision keeps the values the control already had: no token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep tertiary in every enabled state (chosen); B, Figma's secondary at rest and tertiary on focus; C, secondary in every state, rejected because it is too close to the typed value and the same color as the help text. See the Text field's decision for the measurements.

decisions.text: The resting border of the box is global.border.base.neutral.5, as the Text field's (decision border-base-neutral-5 of the Text field, which holds the rule, the options and the measurements): #8C8C8C in light and #9C9C9C in dark, 3.30:1 and 6.40:1 on the page, 3.12:1 and 4.80:1 at the lowest on the surface levels. Hover and read-only keep it. Disabled, the focus outline and the severity outlines are unchanged.

The fill of the box of the Textarea is the page's own level, as the Text field's (decision fill-page-level of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): global.bg.level.0.default at rest, global.bg.level.0.hover on hover, global.bg.level.1.default when read-only. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes. The disabled fill is not decided here.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the page level (chosen); B, Figma's level 1; C, the default Button's translucent subtle fill, rejected because the placeholder fails WCAG 1.4.3 in dark. The fill does not identify the field, the border does. Every form control reads the same fill.

decisions.text: The Textarea draws focus and a severity as the Text field does (decision state-outline-flush of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): the border stays 0.6 px in every state and the outline is drawn flush over it, offset minus the border width, so the text never moves. Focus is an outline of focus.ring.width (2.4 px) in color.focus.ring; a severity (error, warning or success) at rest an outline of stroke-width.md (1.2 px) in the severity's border color; a severity with focus 2.4 px in the severity's color. textarea.control.outline-offset.focus-visible is removed. pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 (E4a at offset minus 0.6 px); see the Text field's decision for the options, the rationale and the known consequences (2.4.13 not met at 1x and 2x, a severity at 1 px at 1x, the focus color broken for a severity with focus).

decisions.text: The Textarea takes the corner radius of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision radius-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 2 px, medium and large 4 px (textarea.control.border-radius per size). pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check. Changes the single 4 px radius of the Figma-library import; everything else is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options (A, keep 4 px at every size; B, the Shape foundation's radius per size, chosen; C, 2 px at every size); see the Text field's decision for the rationale.

decisions.text: The parts of the Textarea are 6 px apart at every size and in every state (textarea.container.gap, space.4 to space.6), as the Text field's (decision part-gap-6 of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale). pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check. Changes the 4 px gap of the Figma-library import; everything else is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options (A, keep 4 px; B and C, Figma's two inconsistent sets of gaps; D, 6 px everywhere, chosen); see the Text field's decision for the rationale.

decisions.text: The label of the Textarea takes the text size of the value, and the description and the message the helper sizes, as the Text field's (decision label-help-text-sizes of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): label small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px; description and message small 12 px, medium 12 px, large 14 px. Each is a typography token per size. pnpm validate compares textarea.label.typography.*, textarea.description.typography.* and textarea.message.typography.* with the Text field's. Changes the single 14 px style that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep the single 14 px style for the label, the description and the message; B, the label follows the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text stays 14 px; C, the label follows the field and the help text takes Figma's helper sizes (12 / 12 / 14 px), chosen; D, Figma's sizes (label 12 / 14 / 16 px, help text 12 / 12 / 14 px, compact line height), rejected because the label would be smaller than the value at the small size and the Typography foundation would need an exception. A label above a field reads at the field's own size, and the help text is secondary to what it describes.

decisions.text: The inline padding of the box of the Textarea is the inline padding of the Button without an icon, as the Text field's (decision padding-inline-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 8 px, medium 12 px, large 16 px. The block padding stays the Textarea's own. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the inline padding of the Button without an icon (8 / 12 / 16 px), chosen; B, Figma's 6 / 8 / 10 px; C, the Button's label-side padding (8 / 8 / 10 px), rejected here because it belongs to the question of a leading icon in the field. A field and a Button of the same size start their text at the same inset.

decisions.text: The minimum height of the Textarea takes the height of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision box-height-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 28 px, medium 36 px, large 44 px. It is a floor under the rows: at the default three rows the control is taller (three lines and the block padding), so the minimum only governs a Textarea of one row or one resized smaller. pnpm validate compares textarea.control.min-height.* with the Text field's. The block padding and the rows stay the Textarea's own. Changes the 32 / 40 / 48 px minimum heights that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep 32 / 40 / 48 px (one step taller than the Button of the same size); B, the Button's heights 28 / 36 / 44 px, chosen; C, the height Figma's padding gives with the new text (33.6 / 40 / 44 px), which matches neither the Button nor today's; D, Figma's heights rounded up (36 / 40 / 44 px). A field and a Button of the same size line up (a search field next to its button, a form row), and the large size reaches the 44 pt that Apple recommends. The hit region of the small and medium sizes is a later step, as for the Button.

decisions.text: The value and placeholder text of the Textarea takes the text size of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision value-text-button-size of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px, regular weight, normal letter spacing and the tight line height (1.2) of the Text field, which pnpm validate compares with textarea.control.typography.*. The block padding and the rows stay the Textarea's own. Supersedes sizes: the heights, inline padding, border, corners and the 14 px label, description and error message of that decision are unchanged here; only the text of the large size (20 to 16 px) and the line height (1.5 to 1.2) change.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep today's text (small 14, medium 16, large 20 px, line height 1.5: the large size breaks the rule); B, the Button's whole label style (medium weight, compact line height 1.0, tight letter spacing), rejected because people's content would look like a control label, descenders and accents would touch the line, and the Typography foundation would need an exception; C, the Button's text size with the Typography foundation's single-line style (regular weight, normal letter spacing, tight line height 1.2), chosen; D, the Button's text size with the line height 1.5, rejected because that line height is meant for running text. The Textarea, which holds several lines, takes the same 1.2 line height by team decision (step 3b, option A; rejected: B, its own line height 1.5, the foundation's running-text value), the mirror staying whole.

decisions.text: The Textarea always renders the same box as the Text field of the same size and state: height, inline padding, text, border, corners, colors, focus ring, label, description, message and motion are the Text field's, and only its block padding and its rows are its own. A Text field decision on any of these applies to the Textarea in the same change: pnpm validate fails when a Textarea token differs from the Text field token at the same place (MIRRORS in scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, decision field-family-mirrors of the Text field). The mirror covers rendering only: a contract decision is asked for the Textarea too.
decisions.rationale: Nothing tied the three plain fields to the Text field: a decision on its box left them behind. Mirroring them lets every rendering step of the Text field refinement change the four in the same commit, and pnpm validate prove they agree, where the alternatives (the Text field alone, with a closing step per sibling or an issue for the others) leave the siblings out of step in between. The Select is not mirrored now: it gets its own step later, with the complex controls.

decisions.text: The control shows one of three severities, set by the severity property (none by default, error, warning, success): its border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message, the message property shown only with a severity, takes the severity's functional text color. A message carries every severity, in the same part; severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates) and the severity is also data-severity; warning and success have no web state and are said in the message text. The fill, the icon and the message wording of each severity are rendered in Forms step 6. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; read-only takes the level 1 surface; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.
The textarea shows the number of lines of its rows property (three by default), with a block padding of 6, 8 or 12 px by size, and people can resize it vertically; it never resizes horizontally.

changelog.note: Decision error-fill-subtle: a field in error is filled with global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default (new token textarea.control.background.error), at rest and on hover alike; it kept the page-level fill before. Placeholder on the fill 5.42:1 (light) and 6.62:1 (dark), value 16.91:1 and 11.67:1, the error border against it 5.45:1 and 5.14:1.

Decision variants-modeled-differently (Text field decision of the same name): the departures from the Figma prototype are recorded and read-only is kept. New guideline: a read-only field's fill is 1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill, so say that it is read-only in the label or the description. The readonly property and the read-only example say so. No token or rendering change.

Decision placeholder-tertiary (Text field decision of the same name): the placeholder (textarea.control.placeholder-color.*) stays global.text.on-base.neutral.tertiary in every enabled state, rather than Figma's secondary at rest. Distance from the value, light / dark: 3.12:1 / 1.76:1 (secondary 1.48:1 / 1.27:1); contrast against the fill at rest 6.08:1 / 6.40:1 (lowest 5.75:1 / 5.86:1). Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision border-base-neutral-5 (Text field decision of the same name): the resting border of the box (textarea.control.border-color.default) is global.border.base.neutral.5 instead of global.border.accent.neutral.default: #8C8C8C in light (was #313131) and #9C9C9C in dark (was #CFCFCF). Contrast of the border on the surface levels 0 / 1 / 2 / 3: light 3.30 / 3.12 / 3.30 / 3.12:1, dark 6.40 / 5.86 / 5.36 / 4.80:1 (was 12.78 / 12.09 / 12.78 / 12.09:1 and 11.28 / 10.33 / 9.46 / 8.47:1). Disabled, focus and the severities are unchanged.

Decision fill-page-level (Text field decision of the same name): the fill of the box (textarea.control.background.*) stays the page's level, global.bg.level.0.default at rest and .hover on hover, global.bg.level.1.default when read-only. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision state-outline-flush: focus is an outline of 2.4 px (focus.ring.width, color.focus.ring) drawn flush over the 0.6 px border, offset minus the border width, instead of a ring 4 px away; a severity (error, warning, success) is an outline of 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) in the severity's border color (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default), 2.4 px in that color with focus; the border and the text never change; outline-offset.focus-visible removed. Contrast, light / dark: focus outline 5.77:1 / 12.76:1 on the default surface (5.45 / 9.58 on level 3); severity outlines as the severity borders, on the default surface and at least on every surface level: error 6.12:1 / 4.97:1 and 5.79 / 3.73, warning 3.27:1 / 8.09:1 and 3.09 / 6.07, success 7.87:1 / 6.08:1 and 7.44 / 4.57. WCAG 2.4.13 is no longer claimed.

Decision radius-button: the corner radius of the box is the Button's at the same size (textarea.control.border-radius per size: small corner-radius.2xs, 2 px; medium and large corner-radius.xs, 4 px; it was corner-radius.xs, 4 px, at every size). Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision part-gap-6: the parts of the field are 6 px apart at every size and in every state (textarea.container.gap: space.4 to space.6, 4 px to 6 px between the label, the box, the description and the message). The box never moves between states. Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision label-help-text-sizes (Text field decision of the same name): the label scales with the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text shrinks (12 / 12 / 14 px) (textarea.label.typography: one 14 px style becomes small, medium and large, font size body.size.sm to sm / md / md, line height normal 1.5 to tight 1.2; textarea.description.typography and textarea.message.typography: body.size.sm to xs / xs / sm, so 14 px becomes 12 / 12 / 14 px; weights, normal line height and letter spacing kept). The Size property now affects the label, the description and the message. pnpm validate now fails when the label and the value alias different font size tokens. Colors unchanged; contrast re-measured on levels 0 to 3: description 12.78:1 (levels 0 and 2) and 12.09:1 (levels 1 and 3) in light mode, 8.86:1, 8.11:1, 7.43:1 and 6.65:1 on levels 0 to 3 in dark mode; error text 6.12:1 and 5.79:1 (levels 0 and 2, then 1 and 3) in light mode, 7.06:1, 6.47:1, 5.92:1 and 5.30:1 in dark mode, the same on every platform; 4.5:1 required (WCAG 1.4.3), the lowest being 6.65:1 (description) and 5.30:1 (error text).

Decision padding-inline-button (Text field decision of the same name): the inline padding (textarea.control.padding-inline.*) is the Button's inline padding without an icon at the same size. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision box-height-button (Text field decision of the same name): the minimum height takes the height of the Button of the same size (textarea.control.min-height.*: 32 / 40 / 48 px become 28 / 36 / 44 px). Target size (WCAG 2.5.8): every size stays above 24 x 24 CSS px. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision value-text-button-size (Text field decision of the same name): the value and placeholder text takes the text size of the Button of the same size (small 14, medium 16, large 16 px; the large size was 20 px), with the tight line height of the Text field (textarea.control.typography.*: large font size body.size.lg to body.size.md, line height normal to tight). Supersedes sizes. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision same-box-as-text-field (Text field decision field-family-mirrors): the Textarea is a mirror of the Text field, so every Text field decision on the box applies here in the same change and pnpm validate compares the tokens; its block padding is declared as its own. No token, CSS or template change: the tokens already resolve to the Text field's values in every platform and mode, so sizes, colors and contrast are unchanged.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error, warning, success), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error, warning and success; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error, with warning and success and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], textarea__error-message is textarea__message. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821; error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.26 → 5.79:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 6.36 → 6.40:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, label-description-error, rows-and-resize). Native textarea in a wrapper with a label element, a description and an error message; states default, hover, focus-visible, invalid, readonly, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, placeholder 6.08 / 6.36, error text 4.52 / 4.97 (4.26 on level 1 in light mode), border at rest 12.87 / 8.80 and 12.14 / 8.06 on hover, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
